course_name_original: Gestión integrada de la calidad, medio ambiente y riesgos laborales (106569)
course_name_en: Integrated Quality, Environmental, and Occupational Risk Management
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of computing and statistics is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the main methodologies and tools for quality management.
Have basic knowledge of the main tools for statistical process control and capability measurement.
Know and fluently handle regulations concerning Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems, especially the ISO 45001 standard.
Know and fluently handle regulations concerning Quality Management Systems, especially the ISO 9001 standard.
Know and fluently handle regulations concerning Environmental Management Systems, especially the ISO 14001 standard.
Be able to integrate different management systems.
Aptitude for resource and time distribution and its implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability for teamwork and capacity for developing multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Aptitude for professional insertion in diverse environments and with varied functions in the field of Industrial Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Methodologies and tools for Quality Management. Introduction to Quality Control in industrial processes. International standards for Quality Management.
International standards for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems. International standards for Environmental Management. Integration of management systems.
Drafting of Manuals, Procedures, and Work Instructions. Audit Plans
teaching_methods: Lecture and resolution of exercises/practical cases with student participation and specialized software use.
Personal study of theory and problems/practical exercises.
Preparation of practical reports, assignments, and/or problem sets proposed by the professor, including those requiring software use.
Search and consultation of bibliographic information.

Active methodologies will be encouraged, with the possibility of replacing theoretical classes for certain content with virtual sessions and/or synchronous or asynchronous modules to focus on autonomous and teamwork practical work.
Classroom activities (individual and/or group-based) subject to continuous assessment.
Tutorials (in-person or remote via virtual platform, email, or messaging).

assessment_methods.method: Exams (written, in-person or via Virtual Campus)
Supervised practical assignments, seminars, and laboratory work (physical and/or software)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade in the exams, never exceeding 5 out of 10 points, is a necessary but not sufficient condition. Students who do not achieve this minimum grade in the exams will not pass the course, regardless of grades obtained in other continuous assessment elements, with the maximum possible final grade in such a case being 4.5 out of 10 points. For students who achieve this minimum grade in the exams, the final grade will be obtained from the weighted average of each assessment element. If the exams are not passed in the first attempt, the grades obtained in the other assessment elements will be retained for the second attempt. Exceptionally, and when the number of students allows, written evaluation tests in the ordinary session may be replaced by individual projects that must be orally presented, and the student must answer questions from the professor. Students who do not pass the course in the ordinary session must take the final exam in the extraordinary session.
